context:
Work outside-in: start by deleting the leaf Plotly files (charts.py, styles.py, dependencies.py)
that nothing else imports, then strip Plotly code from the shared files (result_plotter.py,
exporters.py, visualization.py) that have both Plotly and ASCII paths. After removal, unify the
data models by promoting ASCII models as canonical and refactoring ResultPlotter to produce them
directly. Finally simplify the MCP/CLI interface by removing format branching.

Key files to reference for understanding the current dual-path architecture:
- exporters.py:render_ascii_chart() - shows the conversion between Plotly and ASCII models
- mcp/tools/visualization.py - shows the format branching (HTML vs ASCII)
- charts.py - the Plotly chart classes that will be deleted entirely
description:
Remove Plotly and the entire HTML chart rendering pipeline from BenchBox. The ASCII charting
system (2,255 lines, 6 chart types, zero dependencies) is the actively-used visualization
path for CLI, MCP, and CI. The Plotly/HTML path (~1,750 lines source + ~1,260 lines tests)
generates static .html files that nobody opens - there is no browser integration, no HTTP
server, no CI usage, and no documented user workflow that depends on HTML output.

Removing Plotly eliminates:
- Two parallel rendering pipelines with incompatible data models
- ~2,300 lines of source + test code (37% reduction in visualization module)
- 46 MB optional dependency weight (plotly 43 MB + narwhals 3.3 MB)
- The dual data model problem (BarDatum vs BarData, etc.) that forces every new chart type
  to be implemented twice
- Three test files that use pytest.importorskip("plotly") and may skip silently

This clears the path for the ASCII charting enhancement (enhance-ascii-charting.yaml) by
establishing a single canonical data model and removing the need for conversion layers.

Decision rationale: Evaluated in depth - HTML charts are the default format but disconnected
from real usage. MCP returns file paths for HTML (useless to LLMs) vs inline content for ASCII
(immediately useful). CLI generates files users must manually locate and open. No blog workflow
references chart generation. The feature is vestigial.

anti_patterns.why: generate_chart must still work; just remove the HTML branch and simplify the response model
export_ascii() and render_ascii_chart() serve the ASCII path; only remove export_figure() and Plotly imports
it contains the data loading and normalization logic (from_sources, NormalizedResult) that ASCII charts depend on
orphaned optional deps confuse users and bloat installs
templates are format-agnostic and drive which charts to generate, not how to render them

preserves.behavior: ASCIIChartBase interface and render() -> str contract must not change
All 6 ASCII chart types (bar, histogram, heatmap, box, line, scatter) must remain fully functional
CLI benchbox visualize command must continue to work (ASCII output)
Chart templates (default, flagship, head_to_head, trends, cost_optimization) must work with ASCII
MCP generate_chart tool must continue to work (ASCII format)
MCP suggest_charts tool must continue to work (format-agnostic logic)
NormalizedResult and NormalizedQuery dataclasses must be preserved (shared data loading)
ResultPlotter.from_sources() must continue loading and normalizing result JSON files

verifications.description: All ASCII chart tests pass unchanged

verifications.expected: all tests pass (some removed, remaining pass)

verifications.description: No references to plotly remain in source code
plotly is not in any pyproject.toml dependency group
